gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-bitter: SF Wonder Comic packs its words dense and tall through the middle, with bowls left open on one side. And Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye, grounds the whole thing with dependable footing.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-fs-epilogue: Crossbars a bit finer than the main stems give SF Wonder Comic a striking, classic snap up top. Epilogue, with its wire-like monoline skeleton, keeps paragraphs feeling curvy and approachable down the page.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-fs-merriweath: Merriweather Sans stands tall, with an e that opens clearly right. SF Wonder Comic supplies the moderately modulated, striking drama up top, while the sans quietly keeps every word sturdy and legible.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-general-sans: Striking and classic up top, SF Wonder Comic keeps a modest, readable weight shift around every curve. General Sans holds a steady pen pressure and a smooth path around every bend, and that smoothness is what ties them.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-epunda-sla: Epunda Slab is dignified, with rounded lowercase forms and a visibly gaping c. SF Wonder Comic adds a striking display voice with medium weight change along each stroke, while the body stays low in contrast.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-fauna-one: Bowls left unfinished on one side give SF Wonder Comic a striking, classic look that earns its keep big and short. Fauna One brings a tall middle band and shallow ascenders for the dignified, literary part.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-glegoo: Dense, tall and striking: SF Wonder Comic leaves bowls unfinished on one side, with a soft shift in weight. Glegoo lets long paragraphs breathe, with big counters and an editorial feel.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-hanuman: Striking and classic, SF Wonder Comic swells its bowls only slightly where they are widest, packing words dense through the middle. Hanuman adds a traditional, refined restraint with its high-waisted lowercase.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-kadwa: SF Wonder Comic carries calm weight variation from stem to serif and a dense, tall middle that gets attention. Kadwa handles the quieter work, with open-ended curves and a larger x-height for the steady reading.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-piazzolla: Stems only a shade heavier than their arms give SF Wonder Comic a mild shimmer of weight across each word. Piazzolla brings lowercase nearly matching its capitals and a pried-open e, so text settles in beneath.
